notes.title: Pre-Demo Update 01/23/2025
notes.notes: Very minor update that allow the full version of the Bloc-Age to load games saved in the upcoming demo version of the Bloc-Age.

notes.title: Update Notes: 12/28/2024
notes.notes: I've been tracking down an error affecting some systems and believe that I have found a solution.  The current working theory is that I was using text data files to store information, but on non-English systems there could be a conversion error from the text data to decimals.  This new update now uses fully binary data files which should work the same no matter what language you have Windows set to.  If you are still seeing any problems, please feel free to contact me through support.

notes.title: Update Notes: 12/19/2024
notes.notes:
I have been tracking an issue that on some systems the timing codes fails, and the game runs at uncontrollable speed.  Throughout the last few builds I have tested different techniques and have not had any success solving the problem.  With this update I have modified the timed codes again and it now includes frame rate clamping (among other changes).  In the Menu Setup\Display you will be able to select the maximum framerate the game will run at.  This will let your system (CPU and GPU) run at less load and should avoid any math errors that might occur on new system due to very high frame rates.

Also, I have included a time test function that will output debug information to a file.  While in game, hold 'Shift' and press 'Backspace' to start the time test.  While the test if being performed, extra information will display on the screen (should take about 10 seconds with framerates clamped at 500 fps).  Once that information is gone the test is done and a file called 'time_test_500.txt' will have been created in you [users]\[user_name]\Saved Games\Atomic Hick Software\BlocAge\ directory.  If you are having the above problem, and you have time please email this file to our Support address.

notes.title: 12/16/2024 Update Notes:
notes.notes:
Bloc-Age: Path of the Oracle – Major Update December 16, 2024

Over 1 year ago the Bloc-Age was released on Steam.  Sadly, due to loss of team member due to lack of interest in the project, lack of funding and being trapped by the original concept of the project, I can truly say the original release was rough.  But I had faith in the potential the Bloc-Age had, so I took what was there, cleaned it up the best I could with what time I had, and release it.   I then returned to the factory full time and in my spare time I continued to update the Bloc-Age as needed.  After many updates I found that the only way to salvage the project was to do a major overhaul of the Bloc-Age, ranging from general under the hood improvements, graphical updates breaking from the original retro-styled concepts that were holding the project back, and better controls.  Following is a checklist of the major changes to the Bloc-Age, and further on will be a detailed explanation of each of the changes.


System:
	- Reduced language support
	- Updated frame rate system
	- Better startup to catch compatibility errors
	- Better culling system for levels
	- Improved setup and input menus
	- Mouse over help text

Graphics:
	- Updated tileset textures for all regions
	- Added glow effects (sky, projectiles, effects, lights...)
	- Added projectile trails
	- Smoother lighting
	- Improved level design and lighting
	- Increased FOV

Control:
	- Added controller support
	- Auto left-hand weapon select


- Reduced language support: As the project has become a pure hobby project with limit people and time, I will only be supporting a few core languages.  This will allow me to provide updates quicker in all the supported languages.  If you feel that there is a language that should be supported, please contact me and if there is a large demand for that language, then it will be added.  Also, there could be some issue with the new 'exe' if you were using a now unsupported language.  If this happens deleting the 'language.txt' file from the '[users]\Saved Games\Atomic Hick Software\BlocAge\' directory will solve the problem.


- Updated frame rate system: A reported problem by some users that the old frame rate system was failing, cause unplayable conditions.  I believe that I found and fixed the issue, but sadly every system that I have access to did not have issue with the old system and therefore I cannot verify that the issue is truly fixed, but the new system will provide smoother gameplay.


- Better startup to catch compatibility errors: Again, due to my limited number of systems to test the project on, some users have found situation where the program crash on startup.  The new startup system should give the user more information on why this is happening and can relate the information back to me so that I can have a better chance of fixing the issues.


- Better culling system for levels: Due to time constraints the original release had no culling in game levels.  Some larger level did experience low frame rates due to this, but now with the new culling system, all level should run at very high frame rates.


- Improved setup and input menu: Both setup and input menus are now organized better to allow you to more quickly find and update the options you need.


- Mouse over help text: Now all menu buttons will display information about what it does at the bottom of the screen.


- Updated tileset textures for all regions: Every texture used to display the levels have been updated.  In some cases, the texture is completely remade, in others that are just improved.


- Added glow effects: This is the first major departure from the style I was going for in the original release.  Initially I was trying to only use hard effects that could have been used in games from the early 90's, but I never felt the look worked.  Now going forward I will be using any effect I feel will make the Bloc-Age the best game it can be.  So now the sky, projectiles, effects, lights, signs all now put off a subtle glow, which I feel enhances the look of the game greatly.


- Added projectile trails: Now projectiles will leave trail.  Again, this is an effect that originally would not have been allowed but adds, I feel, a good look to the game.  Also, this effect will help you track down where attacking enemies are, allowing you to more quickly deal with them.


- Smoother lighting: Originally lighting was intentionally blocky to fit the old-time style of the game, but again the effect never quite worked for me.  Now the lighting is smooth giving the game a more finished look without completely changing the feel of the game.


- Improved level design and lighting: Every level the game has had some changes made (minor to major) from reshaping rooms, adding rooms, removing rooms and adding detail.  Again, due to time constraints at release all level were quickly lit and the brightness was increased.  I was never quite happy with the results, so each level was painstakingly re-lit with enough lights to illuminate the levels, but not so much to wash them out.  Overall, the levels will look darker, but I hope not too dark.  But I've added a brightness control in setup\display to increase the brightness if needed (it will take effect on the next level, this may change with later updates).  Also due to all the changed to all the level, when loading an old, saved game you will be prompted that the levels build is different and would you like to restart the level.  You can try to continue, but it will be best to restart the level.  If you continue with the old build and come across problems, selecting restart from the game menu will do a clean restart of the level and you will be able to continue without issues.


- Increased FOV: The maximum horizontal field of view has been increased to 220 degrees.  If you are using a new extra wide screen monitor, the program will now clamp your FOV to 220 degrees to avoid any display errors due to the monitor aspect ratio.  Also, in setup\display the mouse over help text will display the FOV you are selecting, displaying the vertical FOV first and then the horizontal value next.


- Added controller support: For those who prefer using controllers instead of the keyboard and mouse now have that option.  As someone who does not like using controllers with games like this I have tried my best to get the controller to work with the Bloc-Age (I have played the game with a controller on easy), but I'd love to hear feedback from users who like controllers so that I can try to improve how the controller works and learn more about the preferred usage of controllers.  You will find a new tab in setup for controllers (Gamepad) that has some options which you can adjust.  Also, the controller must be plugged in before starting Bloc-Age for you to have access to the controller in game.  And the in-game HUD overlays have been updated with controller functions along with mouse and keyboard functions.  Controller functions are displayed in ( )'s.  Also, now the program requires Xinput 9.1.0 which should be installed with every version of Windows from 7 onward.  


- Auto left-hand weapon select: Originally you had to select each hands weapon separately.  This took some skill to use, especially in heavy combat.  Now, by default, you only have to select the weapon in your right hand and the computer will select the best weapon to use in your left hand.  It will select low level weapons for the left hand, unless you are out of ammo for them, then it will select something else.  This will make the game play a lot more like a classic early 90's game, but you will still be able to use 2 weapons at one time.  This does not affect how the shield works.  The only drawback is that you will not be able to select powerful combos of 2 high level weapons, but the game is still playable without these combos.  If you would like to use the old system of weapon selection, in setup\gameplay you have the option to disable this feature and then you can select each weapon separately.

notes.title: Update: March 1 2024
notes.notes:
- Added Crosshair Size Selection: in the setup screen you now have the ability to change the size of the in-game crosshairs.

- Added Map Brightness Selection: in the setup screen you can select how bright the un-mapped areas in the local map are.  Originally un-mapped areas were black and may have made it more difficult to read the map.  Now you can change this color from black to bright tan depending on your preferences.

- Fuel Fix: the game is coded with a jetpack that I primarily use during debugging, and it will become a game feature in the future, but at some point in the game the player is given fuel for the jetpack.  This should not happen and has been fixed and any fuel you have is removed.

- General Optimization: on some of the largest level of the game there may have been some slowdown which have been fixed.

notes.title: Update 12/16/2023 Notes
notes.notes:
- Level Updated: to stop players from wandering off into the wilderness areas of the levels trying to find secrets that are not there, I've added glass walls to many of the levels to keep the player on track.  If you saved on one of these level before this update and reload you will see this message: New Level Build. If problems arise press [SHIFT] and [F10] for a clean restart.  Clicking continue should allow you to finish the level without problems.

- Map Updates: the map no longer displays small items (points, health, armor, shields, ammo).  Also, occlusion has been added to scouting, making it harder to find secrets on the map.  Both of these updates are to keep players from abusing the map.  The map is there in case you get lost, you should not be playing the game from the map.

- Hints and Tips:

  - This is a story driven action shooter.  If you are NOT talking to someone or killing enemies, you are NOT playing the game.

  - All levels play out the same (mostly).  Fight enemies, find keys, open doors.  If you are lost, try to find more enemies as they will be guarding keys.

  - The map still shows keys, special items, locked doors, special characters, and exits.

  - Remember RGB: red key first, then green, then blue.

  - World levels are only for travel.  You don't need to kill everything.  Check the local map for 'Yellow Diamonds' and 'Red Xs' and 'Blue Arrows'.

  - If you are looking down from a ledge and see nothing but trees and rock, you don't need to go there and will probably die if you do.

  - If you are moving through the level and you come to a wall that you can't see, you don't need to go that way.

  - Just because there is no invisible wall stopping you doesn't mean there is a secret.

  - Secret walls stand out and look a little different that normal walls.  You don't need the map to find secrets.

  - Enemies drop items.  Dead bodies remain forever.  Run over areas where you've killed enemies to find items.

  - Some items may be hard to see in foliage.  Don't spend too much time trying to find every item.  Try to find more enemies and they will drop items.

  - Animals are easy to kill and drop the same number of items as harder enemies.

  - Try to take out the weakest enemies first (if possible), then while you are dealing with the harder ones, you'll have items to replenish yourself during combat.

  - If you can, try to stay away from melee enemies and don't get surrounded.  It is best to stay mobile.

  - You will probably miss some secrets the first time you play the game.  This is normal for most games.  Try to enjoy the gameplay and not worry about finding all the secrets.  They are not needed to complete the game.

  - It is near impossible to collect all the coins on some level.

notes.title: Update 12/09/2023 Notes
notes.notes:
Local Map:
  - Special character (Quest Givers / Bosses) now show up on the local map as a Yellow Diamonds.
  - Exits now show up on the local map as a Red X.

Main Menus:
  - Added buttons in Setup and Input screens to allow for easier navigation.
  - Cleaned up confusing button text to make the menu more understandable.
  - Removed the need to complete the training level before starting the main game.  If you are having trouble without playing the training level, please go back and try it out.

Game Menus:
  - When starting a new game, the 'Difficulty' screen will display instead of the 'Upgrade' screen.
  - On the 'You Died' menu (while using unlimited saves) you will be able to load the 'Last' save game without going to the main menu.
  - Updated the 'Final Rundown' screen while exiting a level: each type of treasure is now colored depending on how many of each you have found (red - none / yellow - some / green - all).  This will allow you to more quickly assess how well you did before you continue to the next level.

Gameplay:
  - You will receive a minor boost to your health and armor after killing a large number of enemies in a short period of time (easy and medium difficulty only)
  - Increased damage of the first 2 ammo weapon to speed up gameplay in the early levels and make these weapons more useful in later levels.
  - Increased number of armor items dropped by enemies.
  - Tweaked the armor efficiency to balance health pickups.
  - Added backstabbing: you will deal extra damage while attacking an enemy that is running away from you.

HUD:
  - Crosshair will 'pulse' after landing a backstab on an enemy.
  - Added attack direction indication: every time you are damaged, a red block will ping around the crosshair indicating the direction of the attacker.
  - Added low health ping: when your health reached low levels, a ring of red will ping around the crosshair.
  - Keys which you have collected are now displayed on the HUD above the stamina bar.

Level Updates:
  - Minor visual holes in 5 game level have been fixed.
  - If you saved on one of these level before this update and reload you will see this message: New Level Build. If problems arise press [SHIFT] and [F10] for a clean restart.  Clicking continue should allow you to finish the level without problems.

Notes:
  - Default FOV is now set to 70 for new players.  This value can be changed in setup.
  - Color depth is now set to level 3 for new players to give the game a more 'old school' look.  This value can be changed in setup.

notes.title: Update Aug 4 2023: Notes
notes.notes:
- Added mouse wheel support: the mouse wheel will now cycle through weapons for the hand which you have selected.

- Added weapon wheel selector: press and hold one of the hand selection keys to bring up the weapon wheel for that hand.  Then move the mouse to select which weapon you want to equip and release to the hand selection key to equip that weapon.

- Added world map location highlights: the next location you will need to travel to on the world map will show a yellow pulsing shape at that location.  This should allow you to quickly see where you will need to go to complete the main quest.

- Added animal sound effects: there were humans sound effect for the animals in the first release and we were unsure how it would be accepted (it was kind of funny).  It did not go over well, and we are always willing to admit when we were wrong.  So now all the animal types have unique sounds on activation and death.
